centering.desc: Centring is a property of the geometry, not something a component fixes afterwards. The gate measures the painted bounding box (artwork plus half the stroke) and fails when its centre drifts more than {{tolerance}} units from the grid centre. Anchors offsets and padding are deliberately not an accepted fix: they centre a box, not the ink inside it.
centering.measuredOffsetsTitle: Measured offsets — painted centre minus grid centre, in grid units
centering.osdTrioDesc: These three controls used to be typography: a bold plus, a bold minus sign and a regular reset arrow. Besides the mixed weight, a font's ascent and descent are not symmetric, so the arrow inherited a baseline that pushed it visibly low inside its pill. They are now three icons from this specification — same stroke, same grid, centred by geometry.
centering.title: Optical Centring

configuration.desc: A host that wants the whole of ChaSet pinned to one specification does not edit the library. It declares the id externally; the generator bakes the resolved id into both artifacts, so the choice is observable at runtime through ICON_SPEC_ID (web) and ChaSetIcons.specId (desktop).
configuration.envOverrideDesc: Useful for CI matrices that build the same sources under several specifications.
configuration.projectConfigDesc: Commit this next to your package manifest to pin the specification for everyone building the project.
configuration.stepConfigVal: Project-level switch; committed, so the choice travels with the repository.
configuration.stepEnvVal: Highest priority — per shell, per CI job, no file edit.
configuration.stepFallbackVal: Last resort, so a missing switch never breaks a build.
configuration.stepRegistryVal: Library-level default when the host declares nothing.
configuration.title: External Configuration

extensibility.adoptionRatchetDesc: {{total}} hand-authored <svg> site(s) remain in the frozen migration backlog against a budget of {{budget}}. The gate fails when that number grows, so the backlog can only shrink.
extensibility.desc: The registry holds a list of specifications, not a single hard-coded one. A new specification is a new entry with its own grid, stroke and artwork; nothing in either stack needs to change, because both consume whichever entry the configuration selects.
extensibility.excusedFootnote: Parametric vector art has no 24-grid stroke representation, so leaving it inside the budget would make the budget permanently unreachable. It is excluded instead — visibly, and only through a marker that carries a reason and must sit directly above the artwork it excuses. A marker that is unreasoned, dangling, or not attached to a following <svg> fails the gate.
extensibility.excusedNone: None. Every inline artwork site in the repository owes a migration.
extensibility.textGlyphsDesc: {{count}} remaining. Characters such as plus, minus sign and the reset arrow are typography: they inherit weight, size and baseline from surrounding copy — the mechanism behind both defects this specification was written to remove.
extensibility.title: Extending the Specification

gallery.desc: Every icon of the active specification, rendered by name from the generated registry. Adding an icon to the registry makes it appear here on both stacks at once, and the gate refuses a name that has no geometry behind it.
gallery.title: Icon Gallery

grids.desc: A grid pairs a drawing box with the stroke width that box expects, and states the render size it was drawn for. Two grids are declared: the default 24-unit grid for UI icons, drawn for a 16px render, and a dense 10-unit chrome grid whose 1-unit stroke stays hairline on window captions instead of collapsing to a sub-pixel smear.
grids.familiesDesc: A family names icons that render together inside one control. Their grid is then a promise about the control rather than about any single icon, which is what the caption close button broke: every icon involved was individually valid, and the row was still wrong. The gate asserts that no family spans two grids.
grids.gridDesc: {{renderSize}}px is the size this grid was drawn for, where its stroke paints {{stroke}}px — the weight the artwork was proportioned to carry. Under {{floor}}px that stroke is under a pixel and the glyph ships lighter than its artwork declares, so the steps this grid is honest at are {{sizes}}. A size outside that list is not a smaller icon, it is a lighter one — measured rather than banned, because a 2x display forgives it, so the gate lists every reference below its floor and each one is a decision instead of an accident.
grids.sizeRampTitle: Size ramp — one icon, every step of the scale, no hand scaling
grids.title: Grids, Weight & Size

rules.desc: Each rule below is enforced by just check-icons, which also runs inside just gate. A rule that is not machine-checked would only be a slogan, so the enforcement column names the assertion that fails.
rules.title: Governance Rules

specification.desc: Icons are declared once in spec/icons/registry.json and code-generated into both stacks. React renders the element vocabulary natively; Qt receives the same shapes compiled to path data. Neither stack owns artwork of its own, which is what makes the two platforms agree by construction rather than by review.
specification.title: Active Specification

philosophy.desc: ChaSet is part of the ChahuProject ecosystem. In traditional multi-platform apps, Web and Desktop design systems drift apart quickly. ChaSet solves this by establishing a neutral, machine-readable specification and token shard layer that drives both React and Qt simultaneously with pixel-perfect and behavioral parity.
philosophy.nativeErgonomicsDesc: Tailwind CSS v4 & Base UI on React; pure QML Quick Controls on Qt — no electron bloat or foreign wrappers.
philosophy.oneSourceDesc: Design tokens and API contracts reside in spec/ and emit synchronized tokens for Web & Qt.
philosophy.parityGateDesc: CI enforces that all required capabilities and visual rendering match 100% across stacks.

integration.cssTokensDesc: Reference var(--cs-font-sans) and var(--cs-font-mono) when customizing font stacks to preserve the prioritized Chinese fallback chain:
integration.desc: How host applications configure and initialize ChaSet's typography subsystem across desktop and web runtimes.
integration.desktopDesc: Desktop applications initialize the typography system via ChaSet::FontSystem. Two calls in main.cpp select GPU curve rasterization (analytic grayscale coverage, no color fringes, no grid fitting) and inject CJK fallback substitution tables into QFontDatabase to eliminate SimSun bitmap strikes.
integration.envCurve: curve (default): Hardware GPU curve rasterizer (CurveTextRendering, Qt 6.7+). Analytic per-pixel coverage produces crisp anti-aliased glyphs without color fringes or grid fitting, scale-invariant at any DPI. Automatically degrades to qt when a software rasterizer is active.
integration.envDesc: The window-level text rasterization policy is controlled dynamically before startup via the CHASET_TEXT_RENDER environment variable:
integration.envNative: native: Operating-system rasterizer (DirectWrite / CoreText, NativeTextRendering). Kept as an escape hatch: platform engine outputs ClearType subpixel glyphs with red/blue fringes on dark backgrounds.
integration.envQt: qt: Qt glyph outline rasterizer (QtTextRendering). Sampled from platform glyph bitmaps, resulting in softer contrast at UI sizes.
integration.title: Host Integration
integration.webDesc: Web applications in Chromium / browsers automatically inherit grayscale antialiasing (-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased) and CJK fallback chains through CSS variables. Environment variables and C++ initialization do not apply to the Web stack.

ramp.desc: Five script portals, each rendered once per type scale step. The passage never changes inside a block, so strokes can be compared across the whole ramp — including the rounded CJK and Hangul curves that reveal grid fitting first. Sizes follow the type scale and the interface scale, so they are named by token instead of by unit.
ramp.title: Cross-Script Size Ramp

rasterizer.desc: The two stacks reach the same glyph outlines through different rasterizers. Web hands smoothing to Chromium and never fits outlines to the grid; Desktop resolves one policy for the whole process before the first window exists and integrates the outline per pixel on the GPU, which is what keeps strokes anti-aliased and sharp at the same time.
rasterizer.qtValScale: uiScale multiplier on every size token
rasterizer.title: Rasterization Path
rasterizer.webValFitting: None — text shaper follows the outline

spacing.title: Space & Density Standards
spacing.desc: Desktop space aesthetics, spacing scale, information density, and form layout guidelines.

principles.title: Four Laws of Desktop Space Aesthetics
principles.desc: Negative space is a tool to organize visual hierarchy and guide reading rhythm. In desktop software, whitespace never equals dead void. Eliminate meaningless empty hollows and horizontal tearing to preserve order and compact elegance.
principles.law1Desc: Dialog, Sheet, and Card vertical heights default to auto, hugging content snugly. Strictly avoid hardcoding fixed heights when content is minimal, which creates 100px+ dead voids.
principles.law2Desc: Modal dialogs follow Windows 11 WinUI 3 ContentDialog guidelines with vertical top-aligned label stacks. Inputs span full content width on a single elevated surface, strictly avoiding nested cards (No Card-in-Card).
principles.law3Desc: Move away from mobile-style loose p-8/p-6 padding. Core desktop containers converge on p-5 (20px), paired with micro-gap 6px, tight gap 8px, and field gap 14px.
principles.law4Title: Win11 Clean Baseline & No Hard Dividers
principles.law4Desc: Following modern Windows 11 Fluent specifications, dialog footers eliminate hard dividers completely, relying on clean 20px~24px breathing space for functional grouping.

scale.title: Standard Spacing Scale
scale.desc: A unified spacing scale driving exact alignment across both React (rem) and Qt (ThemeTokens.dp).

forms.title: Form Layout Patterns: Win11 Recommended vs Anti-Pattern
forms.desc: Visual comparison illustrating why the Windows 11 WinUI 3 ContentDialog stack pattern provides an authentic desktop native experience.
forms.recPoint1: Direct vertical eye scanning with zero zig-zag across rows
forms.recPoint2: Single elevated surface with zero nested card clutter and zero redundant dividers
forms.recPoint3: Strictly hugs content height (Auto-Hug), 100% aligned with Windows 11 ContentDialog
forms.antiPoint1: Wastes 100px+ of dead space to the left of short labels
forms.antiPoint2: Forces the visual center of gravity rightwards, collapsing layout balance
forms.antiPoint3: Creates severe visual disconnection between title and input field

containers.title: Dialog & Container Size Contract
containers.desc: Distinct container width tiers for different scenarios; vertical height strictly follows the Auto-Hug content principle.

checklist.title: Design & Implementation Checklist
checklist.desc: Verify these 5 golden rules before submitting new components or modifying existing views:
checklist.item1Title: Is the container tightly hugging content (Auto-Hug)?
checklist.item1Desc: Check that modals collapse when content is minimal, preventing 60px+ empty black voids below inputs.
checklist.item2Title: Does it follow Win11 Top-Aligned Stack guidelines?
checklist.item2Desc: Dialog forms follow Win11 standards with Top-Aligned labels, avoiding rigid percentage grids and nested card clutter.
checklist.item3Title: Is padding disciplined to desktop-grade p-5 (20px)?
checklist.item3Desc: Avoid blindly copying mobile p-8 / p-6 padding, maintaining high-density desktop elegance.
checklist.item4Title: Does the footer follow Win11 clean dividerless spacing (Clean Gap)?
checklist.item4Desc: Following Windows 11 guidelines, footers eliminate hard lines in favor of clean 20px~24px gaps.
checklist.item5Desc: Form labels must use the native ChaSet Label primitive, strictly avoiding bare unstyled label tags.
